answer: AI app development is building software where artificial intelligence does part of the work: understanding text or images, answering questions, generating drafts, extracting data or making predictions. It combines normal software engineering with model selection, prompt design, evaluation testing and cost controls.
body:
What we build

New AI products

For founders and product teams, we take an AI product from idea to launch: discovery, prototype, MVP and production. Typical examples include document analysis tools, AI writing and reporting assistants, smart search across specialist content and vertical SaaS products with AI at the core.

AI features in existing software

For businesses that already have a platform, we add AI features customers will use: summaries, smart search, drafting assistants, auto-categorisation, recommendations and conversational help inside the app.

Internal AI tools

Purpose-built tools for one team often pay back fastest: a quoting assistant for estimators, a compliance checker for case managers, a report writer for field staff, or a sales research tool that pulls together everything known about a prospect.

How we make AI software reliable

An AI demo is easy; a product people rely on is not. Our process is designed to find the failure cases early.

  1. Define success first. We agree what good output looks like and collect real examples with correct answers.
  2. Evaluation set. Every version of the system is scored against those examples, so improvements are measured, not guessed.
  3. Design for being wrong. Users can see sources, edit output and flag problems easily.
  4. Guardrails. Input and output checks block unsafe actions, personal information leaks and off-topic responses.
  5. Cost and speed controls. Model routing, caching and limits keep usage costs predictable.
  6. Monitoring. Accuracy samples, usage and feedback are reviewed after launch.

This approach follows the testing, monitoring and human-control practices in the Australian Government’s Guidance for AI Adoption.

Technology stack

LayerTypical choices
FrontendNext.js, React and React Native
BackendNode.js, Python and serverless functions
AI modelsOpenAI, Anthropic Claude, Google Gemini and open-source models, chosen per task
RetrievalVector databases and hybrid search for answers grounded in your data
CloudAWS Sydney, Azure Australia East and Google Cloud Sydney regions
QualityAutomated evaluation, logging, error tracking and analytics

We follow model providers’ guidance in resources such as OpenAI’s platform docs and Anthropic’s Claude documentation, and configure accounts so your data isn’t used to train public models where that option exists.

From idea to launch

  1. Free AI audit to confirm the problem, users and whether custom software is the right answer.
  2. Discovery and prototype in two to three weeks: requirements, evaluation set, architecture and a working prototype on your data.
  3. MVP build in fortnightly sprints with a demo at the end of each.
  4. Staged launch to a small group of users first, with monitoring in place.
  5. Ongoing development and monthly reviews of accuracy, usage and cost.

Security, privacy and ownership

  • Australian hosting by default, with data residency documented
  • Role-based access, so users only see data they are permitted to
  • Privacy by design under the Privacy Act 1988 and the OAIC’s AI product guidance
  • Full ownership of source code, prompts, evaluation data and cloud accounts
  • Handover documentation if you bring development in-house

Build, buy or both?

Not every AI need justifies custom software. If an existing product covers 80% of the job, we’ll tell you, and help you configure it or connect it to your systems through AI integration. Custom development makes sense when AI is core to how you compete, when off-the-shelf tools can’t meet your security or data needs, or when you’ve outgrown no-code tools. Our AI consulting team can compare the options with costs.

For ongoing product work, a dedicated AI development team managed from Melbourne can scale with your roadmap.

Examples of AI apps for Australian businesses

  • Tender and proposal assistant: reads tender documents, extracts requirements and drafts responses from your past bids.
  • Compliance checker: reviews reports or case notes against your rules and flags gaps before submission.
  • Field report writer: turns technicians’ voice notes and photos into formatted job reports.
  • Customer portal assistant: answers account questions inside your customer portal using each customer’s own records.

Each example started as a narrow tool for one team and grew once the first version proved its value.

We also plan for the long term from day one, with clear documentation, automated tests and monitoring, so your AI product stays maintainable as models and requirements change.

Every engagement starts small enough to prove value quickly, and is structured so the work can grow into a full product without starting again.
faqs: How long does it take to build an AI app?
A working prototype on your data usually takes two to three weeks. An MVP ready for real users typically takes six to twelve weeks, depending on scope and integrations.
Which AI model should our app use?

It depends on the task. We test several models from providers such as OpenAI, Anthropic and Google against your real examples, then choose on accuracy, speed, cost and data terms. Apps can also use different models for different steps.
Do we own the AI software you build?
Yes. You own the source code, prompts, evaluation data and the cloud and AI provider accounts, with full documentation.
How do you control the running costs of an AI app?
We use model routing, caching, prompt optimisation and usage limits, and report monthly on AI costs so there are no surprises.
